correctness.rationale: Fix k before taking the density in n. For p^j<=k the local quotient valuation counts the multiples in the window minus one, and for p^j>k the contribution is zero. Subtracting from the Legendre sum for k! leaves nonnegative deficits: none when p^j divides m=k+1, and otherwise one minus the carry from adding m to n-1. Local equality forces all carries at and after the first nonzero digit of m in the retained positions; the respective digit counts are free, a_t, then a_i+1. Thus positive local densities multiply by the Chinese remainder theorem, and k! is attained. With J=floor((log m)^3), the primes up to m/J contribute O((m/J) log m)=o(m/log m); all others have exponent one and give log fractional parts of m/p, with prime divisors of m treated separately. On m/(j+1)<p<m/j, dyadic shells of size u in the fractional part have lengths O(um/j^2) and logarithmic loss growing only linearly in shell index. Brun–Titchmarsh at length at least m^(2/3) bounds total truncation loss by O(eta m/log m); shorter shells are nested toward the endpoint in a union of length O(m^(2/3)) per j and cost O(J m^(2/3) log m). Here eta=(log m)^(-2). For bounded truncated log values at the jumps, the variation is O(J log(1/eta)); partial summation with the stated PNT error replaces the prime sum by m/log m times its integral up to o(m/log m). The integral tail and clipping costs are O(1/J) and O(eta) by summing (j+u)^(-2). Integration by parts of log(u)/(j+u)^2 gives -log(1+1/j)/j, with the zero boundary term made finite using 1/j-1/(j+u). Replacing m by k does not change the limit.
residual_risks: The finite calculation checks the maximum and density normalization, not the infinite limit. The latter uses the stated classical PNT and short-interval Brun–Titchmarsh bounds. The uploaded verifier was not executed.
